newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp disappoints, but still a buy.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp disappoints, but still a buy.

text.p: Singapore's Sembawang Corporation Ltd reported weaker than expected 1996 earnings on Thursday but analysts said they were hopeful the worst was over for the diversified maritime conglomerate.
SembCorp's net profits tumbled 25.2 percent to Singapore $30.07 million for year ended December 31, 1996 while turnover rose 25.4 percent to S$1.5 billion.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publication's Estimate Directory, a consensus forecast was a profit of S$38.1 million.

SembCorp said in a statement accompanying the results that difficult shiprepair and engineering markets dampened profits and the company expected to perform better this year despite the continued competitive market.
Analysts told Reuters the group's performance was disappointing, with its engineering and construction units faring worse than expected.
SembCorp's engineering and construction saw pre-tax profit of S$8.1 million againsts S$10.36 million in 1995.
"Engineering was a let down," said an analyst with a local brokerage house.
However, there was optimism about the company's future.
"It seems like the worst is over for SembCorp. They appeared to have stemmed losses in the new businesses like internet and media and appeared more focussed in the last six months," said one analyst.
SembCorp reported a net loss of S$12.7 million in new businesses last year against a S$9.2 million loss in the first half of 1996.

Analysts said they would maintain their call for a long term buy on SembCorp because of its diversification into multi-media through SembMedia and plans to redevelop its Admiralty yard as a residential property.

"Longer term prospects will be underpinned by redevelopment of its yard, its utilities and terminalling investments in Pulau Sakra, Singapore and its potential merger with Jurong Shipyard," said an analyst with a European institution.
SembCorp has proposed merging its shipyard-related and offshore engineering businesses with Jurong Shipyard Ltd last November. The merger was expected to be completed early this year.

Analysts said SembCorp shares might come under some selling pressure on Monday, when the Singapore market reopens after the Easter weekend, but that downside was likely to be limmited. Support was pegged at S$7.00.
SembCorp ended S$0.05 down at S$7.40 on a turnover of 14,000 shares on Thursday.
